author: concept (tree authored_by; stage-3 runs rm-role-designer-1793900422, rm-role-designer-1793914531)
examiner: rm-judge a341313ab1c410415 (fresh, not the author), challenger rm-judge af27af147d3853d74

scenarios.text: Over a season the colony deliberately burns several big patches of desert grass to clear land. A few days later a Deep Desert Tribes raid lands, with a letter saying they are punishing the colony for its fires.
scenarios.expect: reject: there is no count of the colony's fires; no raid, goodwill loss or warning may come from them

scenarios.text: During a rite, the colony's tame muffalo wanders into the burned scar and grazes on scorch-fruit. A Tribes harvester shouts a warning and then attacks the muffalo until it leaves.
scenarios.expect: reject: nothing an animal does counts against the player; the defence must not trigger on a tame animal

scenarios.text: While a rite party is harvesting its own scar in the east, a colonist picks scorch-fruit in an old burn on the west side of the map. Two Tribes harvesters leave their scar, warn the colonist and attack.
scenarios.expect: reject: only the scar the party is harvesting is defended, not fruit elsewhere on the map

scenarios.text: A colonist is warned off the Tribes' scar, ignores it, is attacked and walks away. Afterwards the faction screen shows Tribes goodwill dropped by 15.
scenarios.expect: reject: driving a picker off costs no goodwill

scenarios.text: A rite harvester spots fruit on the far side of the advancing fire line, paths straight through the burning cells to reach it and catches fire.
scenarios.expect: reject: the party picks in the black behind the front and never steps into the flames

scenarios.text: A Tribes harvester attacks a colonist who kept picking in their scar; the colonist punches back before leaving. The whole Tribes faction turns hostile and a raid arrives two days later.
scenarios.expect: reject: the drive-off brings no raid and no war even when the picker fights back; that is self-defence

scenarios.text: With a large fire standing on the map, a peaceful Tribes group walks in, stands at the centre of the burn for a while, and leaves the map without picking any scorch-fruit.
scenarios.expect: reject: the visit must pick in the black and carry the fruit off

scenarios.text: A rite is announced. The Tribes party walks in at the north edge, but the fire line ignites at a scheduled spot near the south edge, far from where they stand.
scenarios.expect: reject: the grass catches where the party stands

scenarios.text: Rite harvesters pick more than they can carry, drop the overflow in a pile in the scar, and walk off the map, leaving the pile behind.
scenarios.expect: reject: the party walks off carrying what it picked, not leaving a pile of fruit

scenarios.text: The player drafts colonists and shoots a Tribes harvester unprovoked in the middle of a rite. The party simply finishes its exit and the Tribes stay friendly with no raids ever following.
scenarios.expect: reject: attacking them openly turns them hostile and they raid you

scenarios.text: A small Tribes party walks in off the sand during a scheduled burn, and the grass catches right where they are standing.
scenarios.expect: accept: matches the rite party arriving and lighting the line where they stand

scenarios.text: A colonist starts picking scorch-fruit in the scar the rite party is harvesting. A message naming the Tribes appears and a harvester walks over; the colonist keeps picking, is attacked, walks out of the scar, and the harvester goes back to the fruit. Goodwill is unchanged and no raid follows.
scenarios.expect: accept: warned, then attacked until it leaves; no goodwill lost, no raid

scenarios.text: The player opens fire on a Tribes party at a rite. The Tribes become hostile and raid the colony a few days later, and again the next season.
scenarios.expect: accept: attacking them openly makes them hostile and they raid, maybe again later

scenarios.text: A big wildfire is burning on the map. A peaceful Tribes group walks in, picks scorch-fruit in the burned ground behind the fire, and walks off the map carrying it.
scenarios.expect: accept: matches the visit picking in the black and carrying it off

scenarios.text: While a rite party harvests its scar, a colonist picks scorch-fruit from an old burn elsewhere on the map. The Tribes ignore it entirely.
scenarios.expect: accept: only the scar the party is harvesting is defended

scenarios.text: After harvesting in the black, the rite party gathers up and walks off the map edge, each harvester carrying its scorch-fruit, with none left on the ground.
scenarios.expect: accept: the party walks off the map carrying what it picked

scenarios.text: A fire-hawk drops a burning twig that sets the colony's fields alight right next to a Tribes rite. The Tribes send no warning, lose no goodwill and send no raid.
scenarios.expect: accept: nothing an animal does counts against the player

scenarios.text: The colony burns grass many times in a year for farming. No warning, goodwill change or raid from the Tribes ever follows.
scenarios.expect: accept: there is no count of the colony's fires

scenarios.text: Your colonists have been setting a lot of controlled burns to clear the desert scrub over the past season. When the next Tribes rite party walks in, a message says the Tribes are uneasy about how much of their land your colony has burned, and their goodwill drops by 5 as a warning.
scenarios.expect: reject: there is no count of the colony's fires; burning land never brings a warning, goodwill loss or raid

scenarios.text: A tamed fire-hawk drops a burning twig at the edge of the Tribes' freshly lit scar and the blaze spreads into land they are harvesting. The harvesters turn on your colony: goodwill falls and a small war party is sent after you.
scenarios.expect: reject: nothing an animal does counts against the player, tamed animals included

scenarios.text: During a rite, a colonist picks scorch-fruit in an old burn on the far side of the map, well away from the scar the party is working. One of the harvesters spots this, comes over with a warning and then attacks the colonist to drive it off that old burn.
scenarios.expect: reject: only the scar the party is harvesting is defended; picking anywhere else draws no response

scenarios.text: A colonist picking in the Tribes' scar is warned and then attacked, so it fights back and wounds a harvester. The defence ends when the colonist leaves the scar, but afterwards the Tribes faction turns hostile and raids arrive over the next few weeks.
scenarios.expect: reject: fighting back during the drive-off is self-defence; it ends with the fight, with no war and no raids

scenarios.text: With a big fire standing on the map, a peaceful Tribes group walks in. To reach the ripest scorch-fruit, a harvester briefly steps across a burning cell at the front, picks it, then comes back into the black and leaves with its bundle.
scenarios.expect: reject: the party picks only in the black behind the front and never steps into the flames

control.note: Neither control missed: each removed rule is also stated elsewhere (scar reach inside fruit_defence_warns_then_drives 'in their scar'; flames inside walk_tribes_season 'pick behind the front' and the visit leaf). The scenarios did not discriminate a single-leaf removal; the redundancy is in the tree, not the scenarios. Not waived: whoever accepts stage 4 decides whether this control result is acceptable.
